acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT. Full text in the session log, section 2 / RT3-AC2.

1. WHICH RAW KEY THE DIRECTORY USED IN ROUND 1 VERSUS NOW, AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR A ROUND-1 CONSUMER. INF: round 1 minted from accounts_v2.account_number ('acct#9d4420e3'); now accounts_v2.account_id ('1003') -- two columns of ONE table. COT: round 1 minted from fact_allocations['Account Number'], a MASKED string ('*****4583'); now fact_allocations.AccountID ('acct#7d2371a7'), measured to be the same value space as fact_model_assignment.external_id (837 of 837 distinct values present). CONSEQUENCE: every INF and COT account id in every round-1 directory artifact is a DIFFERENT STRING from the id this cell mints for the same account. The ids did not move because the grammar moved -- the grammar is byte-identical and opaque_firm('49financial') still reproduces fir_c9fc04650e2134d6ea033da2, the id round 1's own fixtures pinned -- they moved because the INPUT changed. A consumer holding a round-1 INF or COT account id holds a handle that now resolves to nothing; a 49F id is unaffected (that firm's key did not change). No production artifact was overwritten by this cell (QA prefixes only), so the exposure is bounded by whatever read the round-1 QA objects; the production first-mint rides IB-rt-6, and whether that needs a migration or a clean mint is a decision this cell does not own. The COT half is the sharper one: a masked string is not a key at all, and any round-1 COT id minted from it could never have joined anything.

2. WHETHER THE SALT/GRAMMAR MAKES AN ID RE-IDENTIFIABLE FROM A PUBLIC KEY SPACE. The grammar is sha256(ID_NAMESPACE|firm|kind|raw)[:24] and ID_NAMESPACE defaults to the LITERAL CONSTANT 'IRPT_DIRECTORY_ID_NS_V1', which lives in source and ships inside the layer: it is a NAMESPACE, NOT A SECRET. An adversary holding the namespace and a candidate key space can re-derive ids by enumeration, and the key spaces are small -- a 10-digit zero-padded account number is 10^10 candidates, and a real adversary confirms a SPECIFIC number already held rather than enumerating blind. So an opaque id is a STABLE HANDLE, not a privacy barrier, against anyone who knows a raw key and the namespace. What it does buy: not guessable from the id alone, carries no upstream structure, and the firm is inside the payload so the same raw key under two firms mints two different ids. ids.py reads IRPT_DIRECTORY_ID_NAMESPACE from the environment, so a SECRET salt is a configuration change and not a code change -- but setting one re-mints every id in the estate, which is the same migration question as head 1, and is why this cell did not set one on its own authority. Collision: 24 hex = 96 bits, birthday bound ~2^48; at 7,480 ids per firm the collision probability is ~1e-24 and _mint is deterministic, so equality is exact rather than probabilistic at these sizes.

3. WHAT THE EQUAL-IDS PROOF CANNOT SHOW ABOUT A CLIENT IN ONE SOURCE AND NOT THE OTHER. The join proves that for every account BOTH producers hold, the ids are the same string. It is SILENT on every account only one producer holds, and those sets are not small: 49F has 17 holdings accounts the directory does not carry and 1,624 directory accounts with no holdings row; COT has 124 holdings accounts absent from the directory; INF has 84 directory accounts with no holdings row. A MISSING account and a MIS-KEYED account are indistinguishable to this arm -- both read as 'not in the join' -- so a systematic drop in either producer would leave arm (b) at 100% of a quietly smaller population. The arm also cannot show the DECLARED KEY IS THE RIGHT KEY: two producers reading the same WRONG field would agree perfectly, and the only defence is raw_keys.json's file:line citation plus its coverage figure, both human-checkable rather than machine-proved. Nor does it reach the CLIENT grain: the join is over account ids, so a client present in the directory and absent from the holdings source, or a household the two builds split differently, is invisible to it. What arm (d) proves about clients is narrower still -- only that the account-vs-relationship grain never widens a permitted set.
